a.text: Your Highness Theresis, Regent of Kazdel, Commanding General of the Military Commission,
Wandering scholars have brought back tales of a new nomadic city on the rise in the distant desert.
The fires of the ancient furnace continue to burn, and the once-scattered mercenaries have flocked to one banner, to the city walls that grow taller by the day.
Your strength and reputation have caught the attention of the Duke of Cavendish.
You have changed the way we view the Sarkaz tribes. Perhaps now is the time to set prejudices aside, and engage in sincere sharing and cooperation that would be beneficial to us both.
I, the Duke of Cavendish, hereby invite you to visit my demesne, where we may sit and parley.
Our venerable empire has use for you and your brave warriors.

steps.text: Winter 1091

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: One more time... I have to do this...

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: No point talking about curing Oripathy, if I can't do something so simple...

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Argh—

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Still no good... *pant* *pant*

steps.name: Field Soldier
steps.text: Excuse me, why don't you put that medkit down? Leave this stuff to us.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: A-Alright...

steps.name: Field Soldier
steps.text: Some time in the gym would do you good, once you've recovered.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: At present, there is no way for you to match the physical prowess of a Terran through training.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Your talents are better employed outside of manual labor.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I know. It's just that, you know, I have my pride too...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You've looked on edge since that day.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I'm thinking about... Theresa.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Traveling alone to a city under enemy control isn't the most logical course of action for a leader.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: The warriors with her may be outstanding, but they're not enough to protect her in the face of an entire army.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The King of Sarkaz enjoys unimaginable status in Sarkaz tradition, and Theresa's own achievements are well-recognized. The Military Commission would not act rashly.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But Victoria's invitation to Kazdel cannot be taken as a sign of goodwill. It means that Terra's powers have once again set their sights on Kazdel.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Theresa needs to go to Kazdel and make it clear that she will not permit Kazdel to become embroiled in another war.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Even if I know how the Military Commission and Babel came into being...

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: In my understanding, the Sarkaz can hardly afford an internal conflict that could drain them of what little resources they have left. They have enough to deal with as it is.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: They have a complicated history, and that brings different attitudes towards outsiders.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The Sarkaz people have a right to choose the path they believe is correct: Theresis's, or Theresa's.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Looks like we've got a lot to deal with besides Oripathy.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: There's a big difference between knowing and understanding, I guess. Looks like there's much I still need to learn about the history of Terra.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: This time, you'll be the one to guide me, Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: ...Of course.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: All we can do right now is make sure that the Oripathy patients at Rhodes Island have access to proper treatment—

steps.name: Field Soldier
steps.text: What's going on—

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: An attack? Now?

steps.name: Grim Royal Court Soldier
steps.text: Word is Her Highness has set out.

steps.name: Grim Royal Court Soldier
steps.text: Listen up! We exalt only Her Highness. Destroy Babel, and she will return to the embrace of Kazdel.

steps.name: Grim Royal Court Soldier
steps.text: If we're branded traitors, so be it. But the Regent must not be hindered at this crucial juncture. Kazdel will take back all that we have lost.

steps.name: Grim Royal Court Soldier
steps.text: May the Sarkaz be united as Her Highness wills.
Scar Market, Kazdel

steps.name: Cold Mercenary
steps.text: Her Highness is coming...

steps.name: Excited Mercenary
steps.text: Her Highness? The one who's still on the run?

spans.text: Highness? The one who's still on the run?

steps.name: Cold Mercenary
steps.text: His or Her, it's not your place to talk shit.

steps.name: Excited Mercenary
steps.text: Hah. Say, did you take that job?

steps.name: Cold Mercenary
steps.text: Wouldn't pass up an opportunity like this if it's the last thing I did. Londinium, that den of scum.

steps.name: Excited Mercenary
steps.text: They say the columns in the Feline palace are covered in gold, and the nobles walk on floors paved with glowing stones.

steps.name: Excited Mercenary
steps.text: *Sarkaz expletive*, capital of a great empire! A commission from a grand duke! There's gonna be so much money!

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: It's been a while, Ascalon.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: It's been so long since you last visited. Why not sit down and catch up for a bit?

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: You're sending mercenaries to Londinium.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Now, now, I must object to that accusation.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: People just follow the money, and it leads to what the Regent has provided in Londinium.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: You're dragging Kazdel into another war.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: 'Dragging Kazdel into another war.' Have you been fooling around with those dreamers at Babel for so long that you've forgotten what it means to be a Sarkaz?

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Since when have the Sarkaz been apart from war?!
The giant's hand lunges forward. Ascalon is surprised to find that she cannot avoid his fist.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: ...Grr.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Seeing the future is hard. Seeing through what you will do next, less so.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Did you think you were the child of destiny, so special that you could bridge the rift between the siblings?

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Think back to the day when you saw them for the first time...

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: When you skinned that young mangler and followed the trail of blood through the wilderness, until you walked into a storm and met the King of Sarkaz...

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: How did you...?

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: 'How did I know?' Are you surprised, Ascalon?

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: I saw the prophecy and led the tribe on the wastes into the storm that day with game. You happened to be the one who lived.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: No one truly understands prophecy. No one can interfere with the future. But I wanted to catch the tail of fate... I wanted to make prophecy.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Theresis didn't kill you. Instead, he kept you and raised you. Maybe he wanted to tempt fate.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: But you never changed, in all these years. You're still that poor, lost child on the wastes.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Have patience, Ascalon.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: You're not a threat to me yet. And I have higher hopes for you than this.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Master said—

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: 'Your blade points at all the enemies of the Sarkaz.'

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Theresis raised you to be a deathmonger, yet you understand less about him than a warmonger like me.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Did you think Theresis would be content to be some puppet for those dukes? Spare your breath, if you don't know the full extent of his plan.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: I'm curious, how would you stand before Theresis, if he was sitting in the room behind me right now?

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: You're simply repeating the words of others, on behalf of the one behind you.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You seem to have put a lot of thought into this war.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: How many hostiles?

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: Exact numbers unclear. We've detected hostiles both in front of and behind us. A lot of them...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Whether it was Theresis's intention or not, the other generals of the Military Commission seem intent to crush Babel while Theresa is absent.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: That way, the Sarkaz won't have a choice.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: How many combat personnel do we have?

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: The best soldiers went into negotiations with Her Highness. A good part of the remaining ones have been assigned to the supply convoys. We only have less than one third of our normal force.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: At the very least, we need to break through the roadblock ahead...

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: ...Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I'll take command.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Doctor?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: If, as you said, this attack was launched by only a few members of the Military Commission, then they're undoubtedly planning to get this done in one go.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: We can't let them set the pace.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Find out where their lines are thin. Disrupt their rhythm, and we'll be safe.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: Have you fought a war before, Dr. {@nickname}?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Not the flesh and blood kind... but I've been trained.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I'm able to reconstruct a battlefield as a computable data model.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Take the front line, Kal'tsit. I know you'll be able to protect us.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Of course.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Welcome to the Scar Market, Your Highness.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Things must be busy here lately.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: No need going against the will of the many. Am I right, Your Highness?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: The voices of the few are worth respecting too.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Many know nothing of what's happening in the lands beyond. Their lives will be turned upside-down. They'll be without a home once again.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: I'm just a humble merchant. My business only stretches so far.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Mercenaries seek to sell their lives. I seek to make money. That's why I always respect the positions of my big clients.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Then I'll talk to your biggest client. The one in the room behind you.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Your Highness should go no further.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Since when have you started meddling in the affairs of Kazdel, Scareye?

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: All the more reason I can't let you go further.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Well...
Please, don't make things difficult for Scareye, Your Highness.
You understand that there's only one way this can go, if you and the Regent come face-to-face here.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: ...Confessarius.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: I beg Your Highness's pardon.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Looks like you've made a decision.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Is this Theresis's position?

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: It is.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: He has decided to abandon our city?

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: Not abandon. Take a step forward, to go on a long expedition away from home, that's all.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: You have made us stagnant. We want to progress.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: The Confessarius is right.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: I still remember when you and General Theresis came here for the first time. Even fate itself stepped aside for the two of you, when you stood together.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: But look at the people here now, when Kazdel is divided.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: You can still command any Sarkaz to your will as their King. You could kill all of us who stand here right now. But why not ask them if they're still willing to follow your dream?
The bustling Scar Market has lost its usual commotion. Scattered mercenaries stow their weapons and stand with heads bowed in reverence.
In their eyes is silence, but the King of Sarkaz hears the voices of their hearts clearly.
Uncertainty, excitement, desire, anger.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Most of you have made up your minds.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Then there is no point for me to try to stop you.
One of the Sarkaz suddenly kneels.
He has not changed his mind. He has not turned away from the temptation of Theresis's plan.
He simply feels a sense of guilt towards Theresa, one of the Six Heroes, their King who rebuilt Kazdel.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: Kneel if you feel you should. Neither General Theresis nor Lord Scareye will fault you.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: Ah... this ancient gesture signifies more than just fealty. I am more familiar with its other meaning...

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: Penitence.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: ...Qui'sartuštaj.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Have you found the meaning of your name?

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: Not yet, Your Highness.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Then forgive their sins as you must forgive yours.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Theresis and I will carry all your sins.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: As you bid.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: I bow to you, King of Sarkaz.
In millennia of Sarkaz history, it has always been an honor for warriors to go to war with their Kings.
They have tasted struggle and glory, picked themselves up from the bloodied soil...
For the Kings of Sarkaz always stood in front of them, never abandoning their people.
Where the Kings point, that is where home is, where cities will emerge from the earth.
Now, though, they have abandoned their King.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I promised a home of peace and safety, where Sarkaz will be forever free from war.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Before I set foot here, I had a sliver of hope that perhaps someone would follow me.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: But I saw fire in your eyes.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I saw the city that none of you had seen with your own eyes burn.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: The ancient city comes in many shapes and forms in your eyes.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: A city of desire, a city of hatred, a city of wealth, a city of glory...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You all believe you will plunder what you have longed for in that unfamiliar land.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: That's why I changed my mind. I decided to see Kazdel's bravest warriors off.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Kazdel will embark on a path of conquest for the first time in many years.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I honor you, even though I never wanted you to take this step.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You answered Theresis's call and dove into yet another campaign of hatred.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Death awaits you far away from home.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Yet you still choose to leave our home and go to Londinium.
The sorrowful King of Sarkaz walks among her people, who bow their heads to avoid her gaze.
Yet their determination does not waver, even if it means defying the King.
'We're going.' 'We're going.'
Voices rise and fall, as though the warriors are singing an elegy for themselves as they go to death.

steps.name: Unnamed Mercenary
steps.text: We exalt Your Highness, but we cannot follow you anymore.

steps.name: Decorated Mercenary
steps.text: The Regent promises that Londinium will be a new start.

steps.name: Sobbing Mercenary
steps.text: There lies the Sarkaz future.

steps.name: Loud Mercenary
steps.text: There lies our future!

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Take care of yourselves, my warriors.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Even if you will never return to Kazdel.
The white figure passes through the parted crowd. The King's people are unmoved by her words.
They no longer follow the King they once exalted.
The other possibility for her people, the home full of flowers that she strived to build, did not come in time for the Sarkaz.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: General...

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: You knew this day would come.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: What do you think?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Hesitate, and all we've worked for will be for naught.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Her Highness did not hesitate. Neither should we.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Make your preparations, then, Manfred.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Do not forget the feelings that burn within you, here and now.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: No matter what they are.
Secret Entrance of Scar Market, Kazdel

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: No need to be down, Ascalon.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: More will join us when Babel grows strong enough to provide shelter for more people.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: We're being followed.
Your Highness—!

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Wait, Ascalon. She's not hostile.
Whoa, that was a hard hit. Is that a sleeve-blade?
Anyway, Your Highness, I would like to leave with you, if that's okay with you.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Thank you. What's your name?
Julie.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: A nice name. One that's not often used by mercenaries. Did you make it up yourself?

steps.name: Julie
steps.text: No... I don't have a name. Someone else gave it to me. She said having a name gives one a sense of belonging.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: She's right.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Why not follow the rest of them to Londinium?

steps.name: Julie
steps.text: I've had enough of fighting. She says Your Highness will bring about a life where we don't have to fight anymore. That's why I came to check it out for her.

steps.name: Julie
steps.text: I wanted to challenge you before deciding whether to go with you, but I didn't even have the guts to raise my sword when you stood before me.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You're a strong warrior, that's for sure.

steps.name: Julie
steps.text: I wouldn't say that about myself when I'm standing in front of you.

steps.name: Julie
steps.text: At least I can be sure that she wasn't playing me for a fool when she said you were once a great hero of Kazdel.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: A reason so simple it's hard to believe.
The red-haired mercenary scratches her head.

steps.name: Julie
steps.text: Well... I guess I liked the way you talked just now. Not sure I understood most of it, though.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Where's your friend? She can come too.

steps.name: Julie
steps.text: She's already here. Her sword and her clothes... may be a little loose-fitting, though.

steps.name: Julie
steps.text: She was a strong warrior. Felt a little like this one over here.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I'm a little something of a tailor. I could hem it for you.

steps.name: Julie
steps.text: There's no need. I'm used to it.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Let's go, then, Julie.

steps.name: Julie
steps.text: One moment, please, Your Highness.

steps.name: Julie
steps.text: There are other mercenaries here who want to go with you.
Theresa looks toward the dark exit of the Scar Market, and sees a swaying speck of flame.
One speck becomes two, two become three, and many more emerge from the darkness. The first torch-carrying mercenary steps into the sunlight and sees the white figure standing on top of the hill.
He points forward and walks toward Theresa without looking back.
More and more follow him, the line seemingly without end.

steps.name: Julie
steps.text: Just because we're used to battle doesn't mean we're willing to bury ourselves in a campaign with no end in sight. If there's another way to live, many of us are willing to take it.

steps.name: Julie
steps.text: I heard some people are secretly recruiting the willing in Kazdel. There may be some there ready to join us, although the journey through the wilderness would be a tough one...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I'll make arrangements.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Let's go, Julie. We have a lot to do.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: There are plenty of people for us to house, after all.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: You're back.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: They've retreated. Outstanding work, Doctor.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Who...?
A group of medics hurry through the corridor, carrying several stretchers. Kal'tsit turns to block them from the Doctor's sight.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The enemy was essentially making suicide attacks. It was inevitable that there would be casualties as we broke through.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We lost fewer than we had any right to expect.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: How many did we lose?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: There was nothing wrong with how you commanded the operation. You don't need to be involved in the cleanup.

steps.name: Medic
steps.text: Dr. Kal'tsit! We're running low on plasma.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I'll deal with coordination and surgery.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Kal...
The medics have already gone. The Doctor is not sure whether the terrifying scene just now was a figment of the imagination, but the smell of blood simply would not got away.
A sense of dizziness.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I'm able to reconstruct a battlefield as a computable data model.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: But it's not numbers that fight a war.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Living, breathing people are fighting for their survival. How long as it been since I...?

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: Doctor.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: First time seeing the blood and gore?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: ...You could say that.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: We didn't have so many lives to waste in the wars I fought in the past.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: Treat yourself to a sweet drink. It will make you feel better. I speak from experience.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: It's all thanks to your command that we were able to triumph against overwhelming odds.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Are your battles always like this?

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: No, this was one of the easy ones.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: I'll gladly entrust my life to you, if it means our future battles will be so easy.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Is war really the only way?

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: You're not the first to ask that question.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: But this attack is only a sign of things to come. No one knows what the future holds.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: I have great expectations of you, our tactical genius.
The history books would record that the two Sarkaz rulers declared war on each other in the winter of 1091, causing open hostilities to break out between the Military Commission and Babel.
For the Sarkaz themselves, however, the civil war had begun in 1086, when isolated conflicts started to escalate rapidly.
The two centuries of peace that Kazdel had enjoyed have come to an end.
